user_questions.question: Your requirement contains a conflict: 'only the account owner should be able to edit a storefront' vs 'all merchant support agents need to update storefront hours and details from the console'. Which do you want? (A, recommended) The owner is the only user who can edit a Storefront__c record freely; merchant support agents are a scoped exception that may change only the hours (Storefront_Hours_of_Operation__c) and detail fields (Description__c, Phone__c, Status__c, Storefront_Overview__c), through the existing Update Storefront Details / Update Storefront Hours agent actions or a scoped permission set. (B) Agents get full edit access; the owner-only rule does not apply to them. (C) Owner-only with no agent exception. Evidence: Storefront__c internal OWD is Public Read/Write today, and the merchant permission sets grant no Storefront access.
user_questions.simulated_answer: Owner edits storefront record directly; support agents edit hours/details only through the agent actions or a scoped permission set.

skill_friction: Step 5 says 'If you can write a recommendation for the question, you have a basis: do not ask', but lists 'the requirement contradicts itself' and 'the design would change behavior for other callers of a shared component' as examples that require asking. For a self-contradicting requirement a recommendation can almost always be written, so the two rules conflict; I asked once for the contradiction and decided the shared-caller fork (service agents using the update actions) myself.

AskCoworker repeatedly tagged facts as '[Verified: prior session]' even though they came from my own 'Established so far' bullets; the response-handling table says echoed facts are already established, but AskCoworker also invented facts (e.g. stripInaccessible in AgentUpdateStorefrontDetailsActions, 0 DataStreams 'prior session') mixed in with the same tag, so every echoed-looking claim still had to be re-checked.

org-verification.md gives no column names for GenAiPluginFunctionDef / GenAiPlannerFunctionDef link tables, and the one-retry rule meant the agent-topic-to-action linkage could not be verified; a documented query would settle which agents call a shared action.
Tooling ValidationRule does not expose DeveloperName (the name-collision check had to rely on the earlier zero-row query by EntityDefinitionId); the reference could note this.

RUNNER asks to put the temporary draft in {out}/ but the skill's intermediate query-output handling is unspecified; I initially wrote scratch JSON to /tmp (outside out) and then moved scratch files under out and deleted them.
